alts: AS LONG AS THERE’S BEEN JAVASCRIPT, THERE HAVE BEEN ISSUES WITH RECURSION… ▸… of course, that hasn’t been JavaScripts only problem as long as it has been around…
WHY? ▸JavaScript is not tail call optimized

TAIL CALL OPTIMIZATION ▸JavaScript recursive functions need to keep track of where they were called from each time, so they can resume at the correct point ▸Recursive functions stack up on each other ▸The stack builds up and eventually you run out of memory
WHAT? ▸calling the function recursively from within a timeout will clear the stack ▸… or at least that’s how he explained it.

TURNS OUT… ▸Tail call optimization is part of the standard for ES6, yet has not been implemented by most platforms… ▸iOS10 supports it ▸#appleFTW ▸Node > 6.5 supports it ▸Only when running in “harmony” mode ▸run node using the ‘—harmony’ flag ▸full table here: https://kangax.github.io/compat-table/es6/
